stories.headline: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.6-Plus, Its Third Proprietary AI Model in Three Days, With Enhanced Agentic Coding

key_facts.fact: Qwen3.6-Plus is Alibaba's third proprietary, closed-source AI model released within a three-day period, designed to shift from passive assistance to autonomous agentic AI.
The model provides a 1-million-token context window by default and is optimized for the 'capability loop' — perceive, reason, and act within a single workflow.
In frontend and repository-level engineering, Qwen3.6-Plus autonomously plans, tests, and iterates on code to deliver production-ready solutions across the full development lifecycle.
The model will be integrated into Alibaba's Wukong enterprise platform and Qwen App, and is compatible with third-party coding assistants including OpenClaw, Claude Code, and Cline.
Qwen3.6-Plus is available on OpenRouter for free during a limited preview period and can interpret UI screenshots, wireframes, and prototypes to generate functional frontend code.

stories.headline: Arcee Releases Trinity-Large-Thinking, Open-Source 400B MoE Model Ranking #2 on PinchBench Behind Opus 4.6

key_facts.fact: Trinity-Large-Thinking is a 400B total / 13B active mixture-of-experts reasoning model released under Apache 2.0, positioned as the strongest open model released outside China.
The model scores #2 on PinchBench (measuring agentic task capability) behind Opus 4.6, while costing $0.90 per million output tokens — roughly 96% cheaper.
The predecessor Trinity-Large-Preview served 3.37 trillion tokens on OpenRouter in its first 2 months and was the #1 most used open model in the US on OpenRouter's OpenClaw collection.
Trinity-Large-Thinking uses 'thinking' before responding for stronger multi-turn tool calling, better context coherence, and more stable behavior across long-running agent loops.
The model weights are available on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0, with Arcee framing permissive American open weights as necessary for the US to claim AI leadership.

stories.headline: Chinese Chipmakers Capture 41% of Domestic AI Accelerator Market as Nvidia's Share Drops to 55%

key_facts.fact: Chinese GPU and AI chip makers captured nearly 41% of China's AI accelerator server market in 2025, eroding Nvidia's once-dominant position, according to IDC data reviewed by Reuters.
Total shipments of AI accelerator cards by Nvidia, AMD, and Chinese chipmakers reached approximately 4 million units in China in 2025.
Nvidia remained the market leader with around 2.2 million cards shipped (55% share), while AMD held 4% with roughly 160,000 cards.
Huawei led Chinese vendors with approximately 812,000 AI chips shipped (roughly half of domestic shipments), followed by Alibaba's T-Head with 265,000 cards.
Baidu's Kunlunxin and Cambricon each shipped around 116,000 cards, while Hygon, MetaX, and Iluvatar CoreX accounted for 5%, 4%, and 3% of Chinese vendor shipments respectively.

stories.headline: Anthropic Issues 8,000+ DMCA Takedowns to Contain Claude Code Leak as Kairos Agent Mode Revealed

key_facts.fact: Anthropic filed copyright takedown requests that resulted in the removal of more than 8,000 copies and adaptations of Claude Code source code from GitHub.

Anthropic said the DMCA takedown was intended for one repository but reached more than intended because the repo was part of a fork network connected to Anthropic's own public Claude Code repo; they retracted the notice for all except the target repo.

The leaked code revealed 44 unreleased feature flags including KAIROS (autonomous background agent mode), ULTRAPLAN (30-min remote planning), coordinator mode (multi-agent orchestration), and a 'dream mode' for background memory consolidation.

Security researchers mapped three practical attack paths from the readable source: context poisoning via the compaction pipeline, sandbox bypass through shell parsing differentials, and their composition.

A Gartner First Take called the cluster of March incidents at Anthropic a 'systemic signal,' noting this was the second leak in five days after a CMS misconfiguration exposed draft announcements for an unreleased model called Claude Mythos.
An 'undercover mode' module in the leaked source strips AI attribution from git commits with no force-off option, raising concerns about code provenance in regulated industries.

stories.headline: OpenAI Shares Fall Out of Favor on Secondary Market as Investors Pivot to Anthropic

key_facts.fact: OpenAI shares have become almost impossible to unload on the secondary market, with about a half-dozen institutional investors looking to sell about $600 million worth of shares.
Next Round Capital founder Ken Smythe said his secondary marketplace was seeing a drop in demand for OpenAI shares, with hedge funds and VC firms approaching to sell.
Investors are pivoting quickly to Anthropic, OpenAI's biggest competitor, as the preferred AI investment on secondary markets.
The demand drop comes despite OpenAI having just closed a record $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion valuation.

stories.headline: Cognichip Raises $60M Series A to Build AI Models for Chip Design, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan Joins Board

key_facts.fact: Cognichip raised $60 million in a Series A led by Seligman Ventures, with Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan participating and joining the board, bringing total funding to $93 million since 2024.

The company is building a deep learning model trained on chip design data to work alongside engineers, claiming it can reduce chip development costs by more than 75% and cut timelines by more than half.
Advanced chips currently take 3-5 years from conception to mass production, with the design phase alone taking up to two years before physical layout begins.
Cognichip uses its own model trained on chip design data rather than a general-purpose LLM, developing proprietary and synthetic datasets since open chip design data is scarce.
Cognichip competes with incumbents Synopsys and Cadence, as well as startups ChipAgents ($74M extended Series A in February) and Ricursive ($300M Series A in January).

stories.headline: ROCKET Upgrades AlphaFold to Learn From Raw Experimental Data, Published in Nature Methods

key_facts.fact: ROCKET is a new software tool that extends AlphaFold's capabilities to accommodate raw experimental data from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, and electron tomography, published April 1 in Nature Methods.
AlphaFold previously could only use atomic models of data (which take weeks of human effort to build); ROCKET automates the model building from raw data in a fully automated and reliable manner.

ROCKET was built by integrating SFCalculator (which links atomic models to their underlying data) with OpenFold (an open-source version of AlphaFold), by teams from Flatiron Institute, Harvard, Columbia, Cambridge, and other institutions.

ROCKET can jump between different plausible protein conformations in ways unlike traditional methods, enabling better understanding of how proteins change shape when interacting with other molecules — critical for drug design.
The tool will be integrated into PHENIX (widely used structure-determination software), Harvard's SBGrid, and the open-source RS-Station platform.

stories.headline: Intel Plans $15M Additional Investment in SambaNova, Raising CEO Lip-Bu Tan's Stake to 9%

key_facts.fact: Intel plans to invest another $15 million in SambaNova, a chip startup chaired by Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan, which would increase Intel's ownership to 9%, subject to regulatory approval.
The $15M follows a $35 million Intel investment in SambaNova in February, which had boosted Intel's stake from 6.8% to 8.2%.
Reuters identified four Tan-affiliated companies receiving Intel investments: SambaNova, OPAQUE Systems (14% stake valued at ~$41M), EPIC Microsystems (~5% stake), and 3D Glass Solutions.
Late last year, Intel and SambaNova signed a non-binding term sheet for an acquisition that ultimately did not occur.
SambaNova said 2025 was its record-breaking year and that it has shifted focus to AI inference computing, with 'new financing around this transition' and a new chip.

stories.headline: OpenRouter in Talks to Raise $120M at $1.3B Valuation Led by CapitalG, Revenue Hits $50M+ ARR

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter is in talks to raise $120 million led by CapitalG at a $1.3 billion post-money valuation, which would more than double its valuation from the last funding round.
OpenRouter now has more than $50 million in annualized revenue, up from $10 million+ in October — a roughly 5x increase in about six months.
The platform helps developers access more than 300 AI models through a single API, positioning it as a key multi-model aggregation layer in the AI ecosystem.

stories.headline: Zhipu AI Launches GLM-5V-Turbo, a Native Multimodal Vision Coding Model With 200K Context

key_facts.fact: Zhipu AI (Z.ai) released GLM-5V-Turbo, a vision coding model that natively processes images, videos, design drafts, and document layouts to generate code, using a CogViT vision encoder and MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) architecture.

The model supports a 200K context window with up to 128K output tokens for repository-scale tasks, and was trained with 30+ task joint reinforcement learning to avoid the 'see-saw' effect between visual and coding capabilities.
GLM-5V-Turbo is specifically optimized for OpenClaw and Claude Code agentic workflows, enabling the 'perceive, plan, execute' loop for autonomous environment interaction.
The model achieves SOTA performance on specialized benchmarks including CC-Bench-V2 (multimodal coding) and ZClawBench (OpenClaw GUI agent scenarios).

stories.headline: SpaceX Files Confidentially for IPO Targeting $1.75T Valuation, Could Raise Over $50B

key_facts.fact: SpaceX has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering, setting the stage for what could become the largest stock market listing on record.
SpaceX could seek to raise more than $50 billion, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record IPO.
The valuation of more than $1.75 trillion comes after SpaceX merged with Musk's AI startup xAI, which valued the rocket company at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion.
SpaceX has selected five lead banks — Bank of America, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, and Morgan Stanley — with 21 banks total involved in the deal code-named 'Project Apex'.
SpaceX is hosting an analyst day on April 21 and offering analysts an optional visit to xAI's 'Macrohard' data center in Memphis on April 23.
SpaceX generated about $8 billion in profit on $15-16 billion in revenue last year, with Starlink having 9 million subscribers.

stories.headline: Intel Pays $14.2B to Buy Back Apollo's 49% Stake in Ireland Fab 34, Plans $6.5B in New Debt

key_facts.fact: Intel agreed to repurchase Apollo Global Management's 49% stake in the Fab 34 joint venture in Ireland for $14.2 billion, restoring full ownership.
Apollo originally purchased the 49% stake in 2024 for $11.2 billion, meaning it earned a $3 billion premium in roughly 18 months.
Intel plans to finance the buyback through available cash and approximately $6.5 billion in new debt.
Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland manufactures semiconductors using Intel 4 and Intel 3 process technologies and is Intel's first high-volume EUV lithography facility.
Intel shares closed up nearly 9% on the news.

stories.headline: Iranian Strike Damages AWS Data Center in Bahrain, Fourth Attack on Amazon Cloud Facilities

key_facts.fact: Amazon's cloud business in Bahrain was damaged by an Iranian strike on April 1, the fourth time AWS facilities in the Middle East have been hit.
The strike came one day after Iran's IRGC threatened to target American tech companies, with strikes to start on April 1 at 8 p.m. Iran time.
Bahrain's Ministry of Interior confirmed civil defense was 'extinguishing a fire in a facility of a company as a result of the Iranian aggression' without naming the company.
The attacks mark the first time the data centers of an American tech giant have been targeted in military action.
The British embassy in Saudi Arabia warned UK nationals to avoid U.S.-linked businesses, organisations, and facilities in the nation.

stories.headline: Amazon in Talks to Acquire Satellite Firm Globalstar for ~$9B to Rival SpaceX's Starlink

key_facts.fact: Amazon is in talks to buy satellite telecom group Globalstar as it builds its low-earth-orbit satellite business to compete with SpaceX's Starlink, according to the Financial Times.
Globalstar shares surged 24% to $85 in extended trading, with a market cap of $8.81 billion as of last close.
Apple's 20% stake in Globalstar, part of a $1.5 billion investment made in 2024, is a complicating factor requiring negotiations between Amazon and Apple.
Amazon's Leo satellite service has about 200 satellites in orbit so far and aims for a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites, while Starlink has over 10,000.
Amazon asked the FCC for more time to meet a deadline requiring it to launch roughly 1,600 satellites by July 2026.

stories.headline: NASA Launches Artemis II, First Crewed Moon Mission in 54 Years, With Four Astronauts

key_facts.fact: NASA's Artemis II mission launched at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026, from Kennedy Space Center, sending four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon.
The crew — commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen — includes the first woman and person of color to go to the moon.
The mission will loop around the moon's far side before returning to Earth; the crew will come within 4,000-6,000 miles of the lunar surface, the closest since Apollo 17 in 1972.
The 322-foot-tall SLS rocket attracted some 400,000 spectators to Florida's Space Coast, with millions more watching online.
The mission will test Orion spacecraft systems for long-duration crewed missions and potentially make the crew the farthest-flung humans in history.

stories.headline: Raspberry Pi Raises Prices Up to $150 Citing 7x LPDDR4 Cost Increase, Launches 3GB Pi 4

key_facts.fact: Raspberry Pi implemented price increases across Pi 4 and Pi 5 variants with 4GB+ memory, citing a sevenfold increase in LPDDR4 DRAM prices over the past year.
Price increases range from $11.25 for 1GB Compute Modules to $150 for the Raspberry Pi 500+ unit, with the 16GB Pi 5 increasing by $100 to $299.99.
A new 3GB Raspberry Pi 4 was introduced at $83.75 as a 'right-sized' option for users who don't need more memory.
Eben Upton said memory prices 'won't remain at their current very high level indefinitely' and pledged to reverse increases when costs come down.
Jeff Geerling warned the hobbyist SBC market is 'dying or at least on life support' because LPDDR chips now account for the majority of board cost.

stories.headline: China's 7-Tonne Changying-8 Cargo Drone Completes Maiden Flight, Billed as World's Heaviest

key_facts.fact: China's Changying-8 (CY-8), a 7-tonne-class fixed-wing cargo drone developed by Norinco, completed its maiden flight at Zhengzhou airport on March 31, lasting about 30 minutes.
The CY-8 has a maximum payload of 3.5 tonnes, an 18 cubic metre cargo compartment, and a range of over 3,000 kilometres.
Chinese state media CCTV claimed it is the world's heaviest cargo drone to date, with a length of 17 metres and wingspan of 25 metres.
The drone has both civilian and military applications, including potential use for South China Sea island logistics and supply on the Tibetan Plateau.
The War Zone's Tyler Rogoway commented: 'The U.S. is falling way behind in uncrewed aerial logistics. I can't count how many of these China has in development now.'

stories.headline: Delta Air Lines Picks Amazon Leo Over SpaceX Starlink for In-Flight WiFi on 500 Aircraft

key_facts.fact: Delta Air Lines chose Amazon's LEO satellite network over SpaceX's Starlink to power in-flight WiFi, with installations beginning on 500 aircraft starting in 2028.
Delta CEO Ed Bastian said 'This agreement gives us the best, fastest and most cost-effective technology available to better connect the world.'
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said Leo was designed to provide high-speed internet to billions of people without reliable connectivity.
Other major carriers including United Airlines, IAG, and Lufthansa Group have selected Starlink, making Delta's Amazon choice a notable counter-move.
Delta plans to integrate Amazon Leo with its Delta Sync digital platform, linking WiFi, seatback entertainment and personalized content through SkyMiles profiles.

stories.headline: Super Micro Co-Founder Pleads Not Guilty to Smuggling Nvidia Servers to China

key_facts.fact: Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan 'Wally' Liaw and contractor Ting-Wei 'Willy' Sun both pleaded not guilty in a New York City courtroom to charges of illegally shipping Nvidia-powered servers to China.
The case involves alleged smuggling of billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia-powered servers to China in violation of U.S. export controls.
Liaw has stepped down from Super Micro's board following the indictment.

stories.headline: Trump Says Iran War Objectives 'Nearing Completion,' Threatens NATO Exit as Markets Reverse

key_facts.fact: In a prime-time address to the nation on April 1, Trump said Iran war 'core strategic objectives are nearing completion,' citing degradation of Iran's missiles, drones, and navy.
Trump said the US will hit Iran 'extremely hard' over the next two to three weeks and will complete its military mission 'very shortly.'
Trump signaled the US would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying countries that rely on it 'must take care of that passage' and 'grab it and cherish it.'
Trump told Britain's Telegraph he could attempt to pull the US out of NATO, frustrated at allies for declining to join the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Crude oil futures spiked more than 5% after Trump's speech while stock futures slid, reversing an earlier rally that had been driven by hopes the war might conclude soon.
Earlier on April 1, Trump claimed Iran's president had asked for a ceasefire; Tehran denied the claim.

stories.headline: IEA Warns April Oil Losses Will Double, Calls Current Crisis Worst in History at 12M Barrels Per Day Lost

key_facts.fact: IEA Chief Fatih Birol said April oil losses will be twice the loss of March, as cargo ships that transited the Strait of Hormuz before the war have now been depleted.
The current crisis has caused a loss of 12 million barrels per day — more than the 1973 and 1979 oil crises combined, which each lost about 5 million bpd.
The IEA is weighing another release of strategic oil reserves after member countries already released a record 400 million barrels in March.
Brent crude surged more than 60% in March, the biggest monthly price gain since records began in the 1980s; Axios reported oil could hit $200/barrel if Hormuz remains closed.
Birol identified jet fuel and diesel as the biggest shortages, already hitting Asia with impacts expected in Europe by April or early May.
Birol called the current crisis the biggest energy disruption in history, exceeding the combined impact of three previous major crises including the 2022 Russian gas disruption.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Eli Lilly's Foundayo, First Oral Non-Peptide GLP-1 Pill for Weight Loss at $149/Month

key_facts.fact: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) on April 1 for adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related medical problems, making it the first oral non-peptide GLP-1 receptor agonist for weight loss.
In the ATTAIN-1 trial, patients on the highest dose lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4% body weight) compared to 2.2 pounds (0.9%) with placebo over 72 weeks.
Foundayo can be taken any time of day without food or water restrictions, a key advantage over competing oral GLP-1 treatments.
Pricing starts at $25/month with commercial insurance and $149/month for self-pay; available via LillyDirect starting April 6, then retail pharmacies.
The drug was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical and licensed by Lilly in 2018; it is Lilly's second FDA-approved obesity medicine alongside injectable Zepbound (tirzepatide).
Lilly has submitted orforglipron for weight management and/or type 2 diabetes in more than 40 countries.

stories.headline: Solana DeFi Platform Drift Protocol Suffers $270M+ Exploit via Compromised Admin Key

key_facts.fact: Drift Protocol, a decentralized exchange on Solana, confirmed an active attack on April 1, with over $270 million in assets transferred to a suspicious wallet.
The attacker swapped stolen assets into USDC, then bridged to Ethereum to buy ETH; by the time of tracking, 19,913 ETH ($42.6 million) had been purchased.
The exploit reportedly stemmed from a single compromised admin key; the attacker returned for additional funds two hours after the initial hack.
Drift suspended all deposits and withdrawals and said it was coordinating with multiple security firms, bridges, and exchanges to contain the incident.
The exploit is one of the largest DeFi hacks of 2026, with total losses estimated between $270M and $285M.

stories.headline: FBI Declares China-Linked Hack of Surveillance System a 'Major Incident' Posing National Security Risk

key_facts.fact: The FBI declared a recent China-linked cyber intrusion into a sensitive agency surveillance system a 'major incident' under federal data security law, one of the most serious determinations the bureau can make.
The compromised system contained pen register and trap-and-trace surveillance returns — data showing who communicated with whom under active FBI investigations.
The FBI first told Congress on March 4 that it was investigating suspicious activity on an internal system containing 'law enforcement sensitive information.'
A 'major incident' designation means the breach poses significant risks to U.S. national security and triggers mandatory notification to Congress and other federal oversight bodies.
